common_errors: Using a simple average of centroids instead of an area-weighted average.
Measuring centroid coordinates from different reference axes for different sub-shapes.
Swapping x and y coordinates when summing moments.
procedure.concept: The centroid of a composite shape is the area-weighted average position of all its parts. Each sub-shape contributes to the overall centroid in proportion to its area — larger areas pull the centroid toward them.

formula.notation: x̄ = ΣAᵢxᵢ / ΣAᵢ   and   ȳ = ΣAᵢyᵢ / ΣAᵢ

variables.meaning: centroid coordinates of the composite shape
centroid coordinates of sub-shape i from the reference axis

procedure: Divide the composite shape into simple sub-shapes (rectangles, circles, triangles).
Identify the reference axis (usually the bottom-left corner or a specified origin).
Calculate the area Aᵢ of each sub-shape.
Locate the centroid (xᵢ, yᵢ) of each sub-shape from the reference axis.
Compute the moment for each sub-shape: Aᵢxᵢ and Aᵢyᵢ.
Sum all moments: ΣAᵢxᵢ and ΣAᵢyᵢ.
Divide: x̄ = ΣAᵢxᵢ / ΣAᵢ and ȳ = ΣAᵢyᵢ / ΣAᵢ.

worked_example.prompt: A composite shape consists of a 4m × 2m rectangle with a 2m × 2m square left-aligned on top. The origin is at the lower-left corner of the rectangle. The rectangle spans 0 ≤ x ≤ 4 m and 0 ≤ y ≤ 2 m; the square spans 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 m and 2 ≤ y ≤ 4 m. Find the centroid of the composite shape.
solution_steps: Sub-shape 1 (rectangle): A₁ = 4 × 2 = 8 m². Centroid: x₁ = 2m, y₁ = 1m.
Sub-shape 2 (square): A₂ = 2 × 2 = 4 m². Centroid: x₂ = 1m, y₂ = 3m.
